This Week's Groundwork

The family's steps toward an order for your husband's care: nine actions, with a line for who does each and by when.

Download PDF

The goal for the week: the decisions are listed, each date has been checked with the person who gave it, every open question has someone to take it to, and the family's offers of help are written down.

The actions are in order, and none of them is a care decision. Put a name and a day beside each one once that person has said yes, and tick it when it's done.

ActionWhoBy whenDone
1. Put the assessment findings you've been given, and the questions still open, in one place.
2. Write down every decision the family is facing, one per line. Keep the tasks and errands on a separate page.
3. Under each decision, list what has to be done or found out before it can be made.
4. Beside each date, write who gave it. Check any date you aren't sure of with that person.
5. Beside each open question, write who can answer it: his doctor or nurse, the pharmacist, the social worker or your care consultant. Note who in the family will ask.
6. Go through the tasks and mark each one: this week, later, or waiting on something else.
7. Ask each person who has offered to help which tasks they're willing to take, and who could step in for the ones that can't be missed. Write down what they say.
8. Look at how many tasks have your own name beside them. Mark the ones you'd hand over if someone offered.
9. Ask your husband who he wants to see these pages, and share them with those people.

Scroll sideways to see every column, or print this page to fill it in.

You're done when

The decisions are listed, each date has the name of the person who gave it, every open question has someone to take it to, and the tasks people have agreed to are written beside their names. Putting the decisions themselves in order, and making any of them, isn't on this list. That part rests on your husband's whole situation and on the professionals who review it, and it isn't the family's to do alone.

If the week goes sideways

  • A task with no name beside it can stay that way for now. Don't fill it in for someone who hasn't said yes.
  • If you can't reach the person who gave a date, write “not confirmed” beside it and keep going.
  • If something about your husband himself worries you this week, it doesn't belong on this list. Tell his nurse or his doctor.

What this plan doesn't do

It organizes the family's part of the week. It doesn't put the care decisions in order, make any of them, or confirm that an arrangement is safe. Those belong with the professionals who review his situation.
